output:
function F(a, limit, sm, pr: integer): integer;
begin
  if (a = limit) and (sm <= 1) and (pr <=1) then
    Result := 1
  else if (a > limit) or(sm > 1) or (pr > 1) then
    Result := 0
  else
    Result := F(a+1, limit, sm+1, 0) + F(a+2, limit, sm+1, 0) + 
      F(a*2, limit, 0, pr+1) + F(a*3, limit, 0, pr+1)
end;

begin
  Print(F(1, 22, 0, 0));
end.

output:
function IsSafe(board: array of integer; row, col: integer): boolean;
begin
  Result := True; // Assume position is safe
  for var i := 0 to row - 1 do
    if (board[i] = col) or            // Check vertical
       (board[i] - i = col - row) or  // Check diagonal /
       (board[i] + i = col + row) then // Check diagonal \
    begin
      Result := False; // Conflict found
      exit; 
    end;
end;

procedure SolveNQueens(board: array of integer; row: integer);
begin
  if row = 8 then // All queens placed successfully
    board.Println
  else
    for var col := 0 to 7 do
      if IsSafe(board, row, col) then
      begin
        board[row] := col; // Place queen at row
        SolveNQueens(board, row + 1); // Recursive call for next row
      end;
end;

begin
  var board := [0] * 8; 
  SolveNQueens(board, 0); // Start from first row (0)
end.

Write a PascalABC.NET program that groups words by length and counts them. Use GroupBy and Each to create a dictionary of word lengths and their frequencies.
output:
begin  
  var s := 'once upon a time there lived a programmer';
  s.ToWords
   .GroupBy(word -> word.Length)
   .Each(word -> word.Count)
   .OrderBy(kv -> kv.Key)
   .PrintLines(kv -> $'{kv.Key}-letter words - {kv.Value} pcs')
end.
